Use cases and client testimonials

What an agent can take off your week.

Two testimonials, and four jobs an agent can take over.

What Jehan and Patrick say about Archie.

Published with their permission. Coleman is the name Patrick gave the agent Archie runs for him; you name your own.

As a small business owner with ADHD, I was constantly feeling overwhelmed and struggling to keep up with an endless to-do list and client communications. Archie has helped me streamline everything with such ease, keeping me on track and helping me get more organized both professionally and personally. It’s freed up so much time, energy, and mental clutter. What used to take me 2-3 hours a day is now done in minutes and more effectively.

Jett and Jack visually walked me through the initial set-up, although it was quite intuitive. Their instructions were clear and they were responsive and supportive every step of the way.

With Archie, everything lives in one place, which I love. Other AI tools feel scattered in comparison, but Archie feels like having my own command center! I can handle my client work, job tasks, learning, habit tracking, creative projects, and personal to-do’s with so much more ease, confidence, and efficiency.

It feels like a huge weight’s been lifted and I’m excited to dive further into Archie and uplevel my life and business!

Jehan Ramadan, Best of Hue Color Analysis

I have been using “Coleman” for approximately 60 days now, and I have found him to be very helpful in my day-to-day life. I use him to assist with both my work and personal life.

Work – Specific Example

In my business, we accept credit cards for recurring charges. In the past, when those transactions failed, I would have to gather each customer’s email address and send individual emails notifying them of the situation.

With Coleman, I can copy and paste each email address, and he constructs the email and prepares an individual message for each customer. Once I approve them, Coleman sends all of the emails. This process saves me hours of work.

Personal – Specific Example

I have given Coleman personal goals that I want to accomplish each day. Coleman reminds me about them and follows up with me to see if I have completed them. I could certainly do this on my own, but having Coleman hold me accountable makes a difference. It is almost like having a personal coach.

I would estimate that I am saving two to three hours per day on ordinary tasks that Coleman now handles for me, including bulk emails, building reports, and generating email responses.

After 60 days, I am continuing to learn more about what Coleman can do each day. As I become more familiar with his capabilities, I am able to delegate more and more tasks to him, which continues to save me time and make my day more efficient.

Patrick West, Chem Can Services · Westway Site Services

Every testimonial here is added by hand, word for word, and a name goes up only once that person has said we may.

We don’t write them for anyone, and we don’t take them down for being unflattering.

Four jobs an agent can take over, and the add-on that does each.

Each is labelled by who it is for, and every line describes what ships today. None of them sends an email until you send it or set a time.

For one person

Your inbox, counted and filed

What leaves your week: Making the same decision about the same sender, every morning.

How: Inbox Rules counts each sender, asks what should happen to them, then files them every morning and says what it moved. It archives and can’t delete. Email Manager drafts a reply for anything that needs one. See both on the shelf →

For one person

The replies and invoices you are owed

What leaves your week: Carrying the list of who never wrote back and which invoice was never paid.

How: Waiting On reads your sent mail for real asks and invoices, checks whether the reply or payment came, and keeps one list with the money first and a chase drafted.

Nothing goes out until you send it or set a time. See it on the shelf →

For one person

Walking in already briefed

What leaves your week: Reading back through a thread in the five minutes before a call.

How: Meeting Prep reads the event off your calendar half an hour ahead: who is coming, and two or three things worth raising. It only reads, and moving anything goes through Calendar Manager, which waits for you. Both, on the shelf →

For a team

The customer nobody answered

What leaves your week: Finding out a customer was missed when they write a second time, angrier.

How: Owed to Customers sweeps the mailboxes your business shares and keeps one row per waiting customer, with anyone who has chased twice at the top.

It checks the shared sent mail first, so a thread a teammate answered from a shared mailbox doesn’t show as owed. In the Archie for Business store.
